<div class="hero"><h1>Resources and training<span class="pill">Draft</span></h1>
<p class="lead">The toolbox is closely tied to the programme's capacity-building work. This page brings together training apps, workshops and sources. It is a draft, and its layout and content will be revised once planned.</p>
<div class="jump"><span class="label">On this page</span><a href="#apps">Training and apps</a><a href="#run">Where to run methods</a><a href="#fpat">FPAT workshops</a><a href="#assessment">From training to assessment</a><a href="#sources">Sources</a></div></div>
<div class="band" id="apps"><h2>Training and apps</h2>
<p class="sub">The <a href="smt.qmd">Stock Monitoring Tool</a> on the iMarine gateway is the main training environment. Trainees run methods there without programming, and use the toolbox pages for each method's data needs, assumptions, diagnostics and misuse risks. The apps lower the entry barrier, and the catalogue pages keep their results interpretable.</p>
<div class="rg"><div class="rc" style="--c:#3a6a93"><span class="kind">No-code app</span><h3><a href="smt.qmd">Stock Monitoring Tool</a></h3><p>FAO R-Shiny app on the iMarine gateway: length-based methods (TropFishR, LBI, LBSPR), surplus production models (SPiCT, JABBA, CMSY) and supporting tools.</p></div><div class="rc" style="--c:#a3604b"><span class="kind">No-code app</span><h3><a href="../data-tools/fishualizer.qmd">FishualizeR</a></h3><p>Data inventory, quality control and exploratory analysis of fishery data; companion to FAO Technical Paper 706.</p></div><div class="rc" style="--c:#4a7358"><span class="kind">Workshop app</span><h3><a href="../methods/multispecies/mmsyfm.qmd">mmsyFM</a></h3><p>Participatory workshops on multispecies MSY, effort caps and closures in mixed fisheries.</p></div><div class="rc" style="--c:#66507f"><span class="kind">Self-paced learning</span><h3>FAO SDG 14.4.1 eLearning</h3><p>Background on the methods behind stock status reporting; linked from each method in the Stock Monitoring Tool.</p></div><div class="rc" style="--c:#94742f"><span class="kind">Workshop app</span><h3><a href="../advice/fpat.qmd">FPAT</a></h3><p>Fishery performance and governance scoring with stakeholders, then the FPAT App to compare management options (FAO TP 737).</p></div></div>
<div class="tablew" style="margin-top:22px"><table><thead><tr><th>Training element</th><th>Apps</th><th>Status</th></tr></thead><tbody>

</div></div>
<div class="band" id="fpat"><h2>From assessment to management: FPAT workshops</h2>
<p class="sub">FAO Technical Paper 737 describes two linked workshops, each about three days, tested in West Africa, Indonesia and Latin America.</p>
<div class="tablew"><table><thead><tr><th>Workshop</th><th>Participants</th><th>Sequence</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>Fishery performance assessment</td><td>3–12 each of harvesters, post-harvest representatives and managers, plus scientists</td><td>Review pre-scored <a href="../methods/empirical/fpi.qmd">FPI and governance metrics</a> by sector, share and compare with reference fisheries, agree 3–8 outcomes to improve, then identify actions and the enabling conditions they change</td></tr>
<tr><td>FPAT App / MSE</td><td>4–12 scientists and technical managers</td><td>Population dynamics basics, app overview, agreeing the input data and feasible measures, historical reconstruction and projections, comparing options against the agreed outcomes, trying alternative datasets, and assigning responsibility for a management plan and data collection</td></tr></tbody></table></div>
<div class="box" style="margin-top:18px"><h3>Lessons from the pilots that apply to any toolbox training</h3><ul>
<li>Agree the basic terms (<i>stock</i>, <i>population</i>, <i>fishery</i>, <i>fishing effort</i>) first, in a dedicated session or pre-reading.</li>
<li>Use a slide overview, then a live demonstration on a case study, then hands-on work in small groups. One-to-one work on the participants' own data teaches more than presentations about data.</li>
<li>Start the MSE session from a summary of the current management system for each stock (size limits, closures, catch limits).</li>
<li>Taking part in a workshop does not by itself build the capacity to lead one, so train facilitators separately.</li></ul></div></div>
<div class="band tint" id="assessment"><h2>From training to assessment</h2>
<p class="sub">Apps are well suited to learning a method and to first screening of a stock. Before results are used for advice, the analysis should meet the same standard as a scripted one.</p>
<div class="box"><ul>
<li>The <a href="../data-tools/index.qmd">data preparation</a> steps have been done on the real data.</li>
<li>The method's <b>misuse prevention</b> checks pass.</li>
<li>The <a href="../guidance/diagnostics.qmd">diagnostics</a> and <a href="../guidance/sensitivity.qmd">sensitivity runs</a> are reported.</li>
<li>The settings and data are saved, so that the run can be repeated, ideally as an R script.</li></ul></div>
<div class="todo">To add: training curricula, course materials and mentoring programmes by region.</div></div>
